subject: Billing lane and co-sell route recommendation: Marketplace vs Private Offer
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@finlytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace vs Private Offer — quick procurement questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the Finlytics team was impressed with the latency numbers. Procurement here is trying to map out the purchase lane. A few quick questions to help us decide whether to take the AWS Marketplace listing route or go straight to a Private Offer / PO: 

- If we buy through the AWS Marketplace listing, when does Redwood invoice us (immediately, monthly in arrears, or on a custom schedule)?
- For Private Offers, how do invoices get routed — Redwood invoice to our PO vs marketplace charge? Which option lets us provide a single PO for the contract?
- Are co-sell credits or partner incentives affected by choosing marketplace vs private offer? Any timing differences on credits?
- Does choosing the marketplace listing limit discounts or contractual customizations (SLA, data residency clauses)?
- Typical timeline: how long does an AWS Marketplace listing take vs setting up a Private Offer and DocuSign?

Our finance lead (cc'd) wants a short summary we can attach to the PO decision packet. If helpful we can hop on a 30-min call — we are targeting a pilot kickoff the week of 6/7.

Thanks,

Maya Singh
Procurement Lead, Finlytics
maya.singh@finlytics.com
[Attachment: Finlytics_SOW_Draft_v1.pdf]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@finlytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace vs Private Offer — quick procurement questions

Hi Maya — great questions, thanks for laying these out. Short answers up front, then a recommended lane and next steps.

Quick summary (high level):
- Marketplace listing: fastest for self-serve, billing flows through AWS (monthly billing tied to AWS account), limited ability to accept a customer PO directly on Redwood invoices; marketplace charges typically appear on the AWS bill and are paid to AWS who remits to us.
- Private Offer (AWS Private Offer / Direct contract): allows Redwood to issue an invoice directly to Finlytics and accept a PO; enables contract customizations (MSA addenda, SLA tweaks) and clearer invoicing for finance teams.
- Co-sell credits: you can get partner/co-sell credits in both lanes, but credit attribution and timing are often cleaner with a Private Offer (co-sell paperwork and partner registration happens upfront). Marketplace purchases can delay credit attribution while reconciliation occurs.
- Timeline: Marketplace listing (if already live) is immediate; if we need to onboard or change listing it can take 1–3 weeks. Private Offer + DocuSign typically 3–10 business days depending on approvals and signatures.

Recommendation: For a pilot with an explicit PO and finance wanting a single Redwood invoice, go Private Offer. We can simultaneously keep the marketplace listing active for later self-serve expansion.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) I will loop in our co-sell ops with a short note (cc'd Lauren) to confirm credit routing.
2) If you want, share the PO target amount and preferred invoice schedule; we will draft a Private Offer and DocuSign packet.
3) We can run marketplace listing tasks in parallel if you want the convenience lane later.

I attached a short internal checklist for Private Offer setup and can send the DocuSign packet once we have the PO header.

Available for a 30-min call tomorrow afternoon (PDT).

Best,

Karthik Iyer
Director, GTM — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@finlytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace vs Private Offer — quick procurement questions

Adding a couple of practical notes from co-sell and billing ops: 

- Co-sell credits: For Private Offer deals, we request that Finlytics includes the HubSpot deal id on the PO or in the DocuSign comments to speed co-sell attribution. Credits are typically applied once the order is invoiced and paid — Private Offers reduce reconciliation latency.
- Invoice routing: If you require Redwood to produce the invoice directly to Finlytics (so you can route to your AP for PO matching), we will set the Private Offer to bill Redwood -> Finlytics per the PO. If you go marketplace, the AWS invoice will be the primary AP artifact and will route through AWS.
- Discounts & custom terms: Private Offer is the better lane for legal/custom terms (e.g., short SLA addendum, data handling note). Marketplace listings have standard T&Cs and limited variance.

Operational ask: If you confirm Private Offer, please provide:
- PO number (or placeholder PO header)
- Bill-to address and remittance details
- Any specific invoicing cadence (net30, net45)

Happy to take this in a 20-min call with your finance lead if that helps.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Partnerships & Co-sell Ops, Redwood Inference
[Internal ref: HubSpot deal 1234567]
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@finlytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T12:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace vs Private Offer — quick procurement questions

Couple implementation notes from the marketplace onboarding side (so you have full visibility):

- If Finlytics wants marketplace billing for the pilot, we can enable it if your AWS account is already linked. That path is quickest but limits legal customizations.
- To publish or update a marketplace listing we need completed listing assets + security attestation; if those are already in our pipeline the change can be live in ~5 business days, otherwise plan 2–3 weeks.
- Private Offer flow: we prepare a private offer in AWS and generate a DocuSign packet for the MSA/Order. I attached our step-by-step Private Offer checklist for procurement and legal.

Attachment: AWS_Private_Offer_Steps.docx (contains required fields and approximate timelines)

Recommendation: start Private Offer drafting today while we run marketplace readiness tasks in parallel. This gives you an accountable invoice and co-sell clarity for the pilot start date.

Evelyn Hart
Partner Programs — GTM Enablement
Redwood Inference

Next steps from our side:

- Attached is the draft SOW for the pilot — please confirm any changes needed for start-of-work.

If you can send DocuSign and the HubSpot deal id to include on the PO, we will turn the PO quickly. Target start: week of 6/7 as discussed.

Appreciate the speedy response.

Tom Delgado
